name: Woodcut / Linocut (Printmaking and Craft Materials). Supplemental design reference, not a directly named style in the source collection.
visualIdentity: Explicitly, this is a carved-print look built from directional cut marks, bold positive-negative shapes, and hatching that follows form. Woodcuts may emphasize grain, while linocuts may favor clean carved masses. Print regions may be revealed, or designed print frames alternated, without replacing carving marks with uniform noise.
suitableUses: Explicitly, single striking images are suited to the style alone. Multi-scene narratives or declarative typography call for a listed hybrid. Listed hybrid uses are folk tales, heritage stories, and book trailers, plus campaign statements and documentary title cards. Inferred: suitability for other subjects is unspecified.
limitations: Explicitly, uniform noise must not replace carving marks. Hybrid with style-030 must avoid its warm palette and soft paper washes. Hybrid with style-093 must drop its red accent, avoid deforming carved glyphs, per-letter springs, and fake wood grain over text, and use carved lettering only at display sizes. Motion patterns should be omitted when the topic is too short for chapters, when transitions obscure causality, or when a cut violates a continuity or loop requirement.
palette: Suggested, not approved: background #F2E6CA and foreground #262820, validated with chroma-js 3.2.0. Their contrast ratio is 12.047, meeting the 4.5 normal-text target as a two-color check only. Gradients are disabled, and the palette stays monochrome, using hatching or screen patterns for tone rather than accent hues. Task-provided exact colors override these tokens, and actual composited frames must be checked.
motionAndInteraction: Explicitly, movement should be smooth and coherent where the action benefits, while deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections, and reading holds are preserved; not every transition needs easing. Video state must derive from seekable composition time. Live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belong only to interactive delivery, which also needs reduced-motion and static states. Optional motion-012 (chaptered scene handoff) and motion-015 (narrative step progression) may be used only if the scene supports their action.
audio: Explicitly unspecified as a requirement. Suggested options include background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence, chosen by topic and objective, with no fixed genre, tempo, instrument, or voice assigned. Speech must stay intelligible and should not compete with narration or essential text. Restrained sound accents may clarify key actions, transitions, or reading holds. User-supplied audio takes priority, and unavailable assets must not be invented.
assetRequirements: The source supplies no approved artwork, typography, or audio asset list. Inputs the template expects include subject, audience and objective, exact copy, duration, aspect ratio, resolution, frame rate, audio or rhythm requirements, and output directory. Optional omitted inputs fall back to documented defaults with stated assumptions. Local fonts and assets must load before rendering, and stateful simulations should be prepared or cached in advance. Python with Pillow may handle preprocessing such as cropping, masks, and textures.
combinations: Explicitly, the style may stand alone for single images. With style-030, it supports character staging and scene beats for folk tales, heritage stories, and book trailers. This hybrid keeps a single dark ink on paper, cut marks that follow form, and consistent character carvings. With style-093, it supports headline typography for campaign statements and documentary title cards. This hybrid stays monochrome, drops the red accent, and moves words in reading order.
productionApproach: Explicitly, the style renderer owns carved paths, masks, and textures, with SVG recommended and Python with Pillow as supporting tools. The motion engine owns trajectories, with GSAP as the paused, seekable timeline used for chaptered patterns and Motion as an optional DOM or SVG layer that needs synchronization checks. HyperFrames is the default pipeline for composition, timing, sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, with the reason recorded. Delivery requires inspecting key frames, watching the full video, and checking dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio sync, and loop continuity. Simulated appearance must not be presented as photographed production.
